nodes.label: Inflation
nodes.sourceDetail: BLS, Consumer Price Index news release for August 2026 (released 2026-09-11): CPI-U all items, 12 months ending August, not seasonally adjusted. Read through a fetch tool because BLS blocks scripted requests.
nodes.description: Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers, all items, 12-month change.

nodes.label: Federal funds rate
nodes.sourceDetail: FOMC statement, 2026-09-16, approved 12-0: target range raised by 1/4 percentage point to 3-3/4 to 4 percent. The baseline is the midpoint of that range.
nodes.description: Federal Open Market Committee target range for the federal funds rate.

nodes.label: 30-year mortgage rate
nodes.sourceDetail: Freddie Mac Primary Mortgage Market Survey, weekly average as of 2026-09-17: 6.95 percent, up from 6.76 percent the prior week. The page shows the latest weekly reading and will change; the cited value is the 2026-09-17 reading.
nodes.description: Weekly average 30-year fixed-rate mortgage rate.

nodes.label: Real GDP growth
nodes.sourceDetail: BEA, GDP (Second Estimate) and Corporate Profits, 2nd Quarter 2026 (released 2026-08-26): real GDP increased at an annual rate of 1.5 percent in Q2; it increased 2.1 percent in Q1. Second estimate, subject to revision.
nodes.description: Real gross domestic product, quarterly change at an annual rate.

nodes.label: Monthly payroll change
nodes.sourceDetail: BLS, Employment Situation for August 2026 (released 2026-09-04): total nonfarm payroll employment increased by 162,000 in August. First published estimate, which BLS later revises. Read through a fetch tool because BLS blocks scripted requests.
nodes.description: Headline change in total nonfarm payroll employment for the month.

nodes.label: Real hourly earnings
nodes.sourceDetail: BLS, Real Earnings for August 2026 (released 2026-09-11): from August 2025 to August 2026, real average hourly earnings decreased 0.3 percent, seasonally adjusted. Read through a fetch tool because BLS blocks scripted requests.
nodes.description: Change in real average hourly earnings of all employees over 12 months.

nodes.label: Household debt
nodes.sourceDetail: New York Fed, Quarterly Report on Household Debt and Credit, Q2 2026 (press release 2026-08-11): total household debt decreased by $13 billion, 0.1 percent, to $18.8 trillion.
nodes.description: Total outstanding U.S. household debt at the end of the quarter.

nodes.label: Personal saving rate
nodes.sourceDetail: BEA, Personal Income and Outlays, July 2026: personal saving was $712.0 billion in July and the personal saving rate, personal saving as a percentage of disposable personal income, was 3.0 percent.
nodes.description: Personal saving as a share of disposable personal income.

nodes.label: Federal debt
nodes.sourceDetail: U.S. Treasury Fiscal Data, Debt to the Penny, record date 2026-08-18: total public debt outstanding $40,047,425,768,420.22, rounded to $40.05 trillion.
nodes.description: Total public debt outstanding.

nodes.label: Federal debt growth
nodes.sourceDetail: No value is stored. It would be derived from two Treasury Debt to the Penny readings twelve months apart, which is a calculation and not a fetched figure, so it is left empty until the interface can show the calculation.
nodes.description: Year-over-year growth in total public debt outstanding.

nodes.label: Net interest outlays
nodes.sourceDetail: CBO, The Budget and Economic Outlook: 2026 to 2036 (2026-02-11), chart 'Total Deficits, Net Outlays for Interest, and Primary Deficits': net interest outlays for 2026 are 3.3 percent of GDP. A projection under laws in place as of January 2026, not an observation. Read from the chart data embedded in the report page; the report's dollar figure for net interest was not read.
nodes.description: CBO projection of federal net interest outlays as a share of GDP.

nodes.label: Labor productivity
nodes.sourceDetail: BLS, Productivity and Costs, second quarter 2026 revised (released 2026-09-03): from the same quarter a year ago, nonfarm business sector labor productivity increased 2.2 percent. Read through a fetch tool because BLS blocks scripted requests.
nodes.description: Nonfarm business sector labor productivity, change from the same quarter a year earlier.

nodes.label: Median household income
nodes.sourceDetail: Census Bureau, Income in the United States: 2025 (P60-289): median household income was $87,460 in 2025, up 2.6 percent from $85,210 in 2024.
nodes.description: Median annual household income.

nodes.label: Official poverty rate
nodes.sourceDetail: Census Bureau, Poverty in the United States: 2025 (P60-290): the official poverty rate fell 0.5 percentage points to 10.2 percent; 34.5 million people were in poverty. This is a different report from the income report cited for median household income.
nodes.description: Share of people below the official poverty threshold.

nodes.label: Food insecurity
nodes.sourceDetail: USDA Economic Research Service, Household Food Security in the United States in 2024: 86.3 percent of households were food secure all year; the remaining 13.7 percent were food insecure at some time during 2024.
nodes.description: Share of U.S. households that were food insecure at some time during the year.

nodes.label: People experiencing homelessness
nodes.sourceDetail: HUD press release on the 2025 Annual Homelessness Assessment Report, Part 1 (2026-05-29): 745,652 people were homeless on a single night in January 2025, a 3 percent decrease since 2024. The figure is taken from the press release; the AHAR Part 1 report is the underlying document.
nodes.description: Point-in-time count of people experiencing homelessness on one night in January.

nodes.label: Confidence in institutions
nodes.sourceDetail: Gallup, 'Confidence in U.S. Institutions Remains Near All-Time Low' (2026-07-13): the share of Americans expressing a great deal or quite a lot of confidence, averaged across 14 core institutions measured each year since 1993, is 27 percent, one point above the record-low average in 2023.
nodes.description: Gallup average confidence across 14 core U.S. institutions.

nodes.label: Trust in media
nodes.sourceDetail: Gallup, 'Trust in Media at New Low of 28% in U.S.' (published 2025-10-02): 28 percent, from a poll conducted Sept. 2-16, 2025, the first reading below 30 percent.
nodes.description: Gallup measure of trust in the mass media.

nodes.label: Reported hate crimes
nodes.sourceDetail: FBI, 'FBI Releases 2025 Reported Crimes in the Nation Statistics' (2026-08-14): reported hate crime incidents decreased 7.0 percent from 11,404 in 2024 to 10,606 in 2025, using a matched-agency trend dataset. The 10,881 incidents also cited on that page are the total submitted, a different count.
nodes.description: Reported hate crime incidents in the FBI trend dataset.

nodes.label: Worker bargaining power
nodes.description: Abstract lever from the solution map. No measured series and no baseline.

edges.claim: Higher policy rates tend to raise mortgage rates, which also track longer-term yields.
Higher policy rates tend to lower inflation, with long lags and a contested size.
Higher policy rates tend to slow growth by raising borrowing costs.
Higher policy rates raise the interest cost of short-term federal borrowing.
Higher rates are commonly argued to raise saving by improving deposit returns.
Higher mortgage rates tend to slow growth in mortgage borrowing.
When prices rise faster than wages, real earnings fall; this is close to an accounting identity.
Higher inflation is commonly argued to erode confidence in institutions.
Faster growth tends to be accompanied by faster job growth.
Stronger growth raises revenue and is commonly argued to slow the rate at which federal debt increases.
Higher productivity growth is commonly argued to support real wage growth over time.
Stronger bargaining power is commonly argued to raise real wages; the size of the effect is contested.
Higher real earnings raise household incomes.
Higher real earnings give households more room to save.
Rising median incomes tend to accompany lower poverty.
Higher poverty tends to accompany more food insecurity.
Higher poverty is one of several factors associated with more homelessness.
Higher debt service is commonly argued to reduce saving.
A larger debt stock raises interest outlays, other things equal.
Lower media trust is commonly argued to lower trust in other institutions.
